feature: Text lands on the grid too
summary: With the grid showing, clicking with the Text tool now drops the text box on the nearest grid crossing instead of exactly where the pointer was, so a caption sits on the graph paper like every shape you draw. Holding Command still places it anywhere you like.
setup: Photonz Next, any document. Flag: A grid to build against, on by default. Nothing changes with the grid off or with Snap to grid unticked.

try.do: Open a blank canvas and switch the grid on: View, Show Grid.
Press T for the Text tool.
Click somewhere clearly between two grid lines and type a word.
Press V, then click the words and read X and Y in Position and Size: both are multiples of the grid spacing.
Press T again and Command-click between two lines, then type: this one stays exactly where you clicked.
Untick Snap to grid in the Canvas section, place one more, and watch it land on the raw pointer again.
Double-click any of the three to re-word it: none of them move.

evaluate: When the caret jumps up to half a cell from where you clicked, does that read as the grid helping, or as the app missing your click?
The box lands on the line, and the letters sit a few points inside it because a line of type is taller than its glyphs. Is that close enough, or do you want the first letter itself on the line?
Text takes no magnet from edges found in the picture, only the grid. Placing a caption next to a border in a screenshot, do you ever want it to jump onto that border?
Is Command the key you reach for to place a caption off the grid, or would you rather the tool never pulled at all?
rough: Only the top left corner is on a line. The box then hugs the words, so its right and bottom edges land wherever the type ends, exactly as they do for a box you resize by hand.
Re-editing existing words never moves them: only a fresh click places anything, and the layer keeps its own origin.
A caption typed on an arrow is placed by the arrow, not by a click, so it is untouched by this.

Verified live: Screen Recording was granted, so both pictures are real captures of the probe app, not offscreen renders. Walk: Scripts/playtest/text-on-the-grid-walk.json, which proves the three landings in numbers (416,288 snapped, 300,505 with Command, 201,611 with snapping off).
